page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes a 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng single-core tests, and average performance in Geekbench single-core and text processing workloads. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks is average at 51.54 GB/sec read and 38.79 GB/sec write, whereas cached small-block read bandwidth is weak.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c2d-standard-4 offers a predictable resource allocation without the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. However, the lack of bundled local storage and weak multi-core performance relative to larger instances suggest it is best suited for workloads that prioritize single-threaded execution or moderate memory capacity. Appropriate workloads include basic text processing, light web serving, single-threaded data compression, and small-scale applications that do not require high parallel processing power or GPU acceleration.
